extracted.intended_audience: general readers; journalists, media researchers, students studying media manipulation or propaganda
extracted.subtask_description: Identify and analyze the 'trading up the chain' marketing/propaganda tactic: how a claim is seeded in low-credibility outlets to be picked up by more authoritative sources, thereby building credibility and spreading disinformation or publicity. Useful for media analysts, journalists, and researchers assessing manipulation campaigns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trading up the chain (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Trading up the chain is a marketing and propaganda tactic of deliberately inducing circular reporting, by seeding a message or claim in a less-credible medium, with the intent of it being quoted and repeated by publications (or people) who appeal to a wider audience. Those more-authoritative sources are then cited, to build up the message's credibility and publicize it further.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording from the page; describes the overall tactic and end goal (credibility and publicity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanism — seeding and circular reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Seeding a message or claim in a less-credible medium so it will be quoted and repeated by publications (or people) who appeal to a wider audience, creating circular reporting where later outlets cite the earlier (less-credible) source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes the operational steps: (1) place claim in low-credibility venue, (2) attract attention from wider-audience publications, (3) have those authoritative sources cited to amplify perceived credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose / intent
rubrics_metrics.description: To build up the message's credibility and publicize it further by having more-authoritative sources repeat and cite the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicitly used both for legitimate marketing/publicity and for manipulative objectives; intent may be promotional or deceptive depending on actors and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uses — disinformation and media manipulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Trading up the chain can be a tactic for disinformation and media manipulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page notes this tactic's application in disinformation campaigns and manipulative media strategies; it has been publicized in contexts of marketing and politics (e.g., Ryan Holiday).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publicized example / attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: The term was publicized by the author and marketer Ryan Holiday, who described its use in marketing and politics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited sources on the page include an Observer article, Ryan Holiday's Trust Me, I'm Lying, and academic discussion (e.g., Donovan; Krafft & Donovan). These function as documented examples and further reading rather than prescriptive rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related tactics / taxonomy context
rubrics_metrics.description: Related concepts listed: Information laundering; Argument from authority; Disinformation; Astroturfing (and more broadly, many propaganda techniques and media manipulation strategies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page situates 'trading up the chain' within a larger set of propaganda techniques and media-manipulation practices — useful for comparative analysis and identifying co-occurring tactics in campaigns.
